decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right; begin mirrored elbow-up right-arm approach, keeping left arm parked. Establish inward-facing gripper before advancing.
Advance right gripper toward holder from its outside, yawing inward with gradual descent; verify rim and finger alignment before closing.
Replan after continuity rejection: hold yaw and use smaller forward/down increments, preserving the accepted elbow-up branch.
Continue slow right-hand side approach toward the holder, gripper open. Keep accepted orientation to avoid wrist-branch discontinuity.
Holder has visibly tipped during approach. Withdraw outward and upward with open fingers to stop pushing it, then reassess recovery grasp.
Recover fallen holder with an overhead body grasp. Raise and move forward while gradually pitching the right wrist downward on its continuous branch.
Zero steps executed on pitch attempt. First ease yaw away from the wrist singularity using very small increments, remaining above the table.
Pitch gradually toward an overhead recovery grasp while lifting clear of the fallen cup. Smaller wrist changes after the yaw adjustment.
Move above the fallen holder and continue pitching down; align jaw closure across its width rather than pushing its end.
Finish overhead orientation and center the right gripper above the holder body before descending.
Descend vertically with open jaws over the fallen holder, keeping its long axis between the fingers.
Seat the fingers slightly lower, close around the holder body, then make a small test lift. Retention must be checked visually.
Lift the grasped holder clear and begin rotating its opening upward. Keep the right gripper commanded closed and inspect retention.
Holder follows the right gripper. Continue turning it upright and bring it closer to the robot for a stable receiving position.
Complete the holder's upright rotation and turn its receiving opening inward, maintaining the closed right grip.
Hold the recovered cup upright with the right hand, turn it inward, and start the left arm's elbow-up approach to the pens.
Right hand keeps the cup upright and stationary. Advance the open left gripper above the cyan marker while gradually pitching for a top-down grasp.
Continue above the cyan marker with clearance, aligning the left jaws across the marker's short dimension. Right hand remains still and closed.
Complete the downward left-gripper orientation above the cyan marker and center over its upper body, leaving vertical clearance.
Lower the open left jaws around the cyan marker's upper body, with a small lateral centering correction. Keep the holder steady.
Seat the left fingers around the cyan marker, close fully, then lift a short distance to check retention while holding the cup upright.
Lift the cyan marker clear and begin turning it vertical, moving back from the other pens. Retention remains to be confirmed from the next RGB view.
Cyan marker remained on the table. Reopen and return over its middle rather than the cap for a lower, better-centered second grasp.
Use the wrist view to realign along the marker and lower farther before closing; the previous lift did not retain it.
Stop descending at the observed contact height. Close the aligned fingers and test a small vertical lift without changing wrist orientation.
Cyan marker now follows the left fingers. Lift clear and rotate toward vertical while retracting within the left workspace.
Rotate the retained cyan marker upright and turn the left gripper inward, approaching above the cup with vertical clearance.
Finish straightening the cyan marker and align its lower end above the holder opening before insertion.
Lower the cyan marker straight into the visible opening, keeping the holder and both wrist orientations fixed.
Release the cyan marker inside the holder and withdraw the left gripper upward and left, checking that the marker stays in the cup.
Cyan marker remains inside the cup. Move the open left hand toward the purple marker, starting the downward grasp orientation with clearance.
Advance above the purple marker and continue rotating the left jaws to align across its width, keeping the filled holder steady.
Finish the top-down orientation over the purple marker and lower toward its middle, with open fingers and the right holder fixed.
Lower open left fingers around the purple marker's body to a deeper grasp height, using the previous cyan grasp as a height guide.
At the observed contact height, close around the purple marker and make a vertical test lift without further descent.
Purple marker follows the left fingers. Lift and retract with it, rotating toward an upright insertion orientation while keeping the right cup steady.
Carry the retained purple marker toward the cup at a safe height, continuing the gradual upright rotation.
Straighten the purple marker over the unoccupied side of the cup opening, maintaining clearance above the cyan marker.
Lower the upright purple marker into the left side of the opening, with a small lateral correction to avoid the cyan marker.
Purple marker tilted on contact with the opening. Lift it clear without releasing, then reassess alignment rather than pushing farther.
Compensate for the purple marker's slip by rotating it back toward vertical in free space, and gently correct the holder's visible lean.
Continue correcting the slipped marker's tilt without releasing; bring the upright cup slightly inward to receive it without crossing the arms.
Stop further wrist rotation at the current tracked pose. Align the marker's lower end with the cup and lower cautiously, moving the cup inward a little.
Replan from the interrupted pose: stop pushing against the cup, release the nearly upright purple marker above the opening, then withdraw left and upward to inspect where it settles.
Purple has settled into the holder beside cyan. Clear the cup with the open left hand and begin a gradual downward reorientation for the white pen.
Move the left hand above the white pen and continue the slow overhead-grasp reorientation. Keep the right grip closed and stationary.
Continue the white-pen approach with clearance. Purple is now visible on the table below the holder and will need a recovery attempt after this pickup.
Finish aligning the left fingers vertically over the white pen, lowering to a pre-grasp height for wrist-view verification.
Center the left jaws slightly toward the white pen in the wrist view and descend slowly to grasp height, keeping the cup steady.
Stop descending at the observed contact height, close the centered left fingers on the white pen, and test retention with a straight lift.
The white pen follows the left fingers. Lift clear and begin rotating it upright, retracting safely before moving over the cup.
Carry the white pen higher toward the cup and continue its upright rotation, keeping the left EE on the left side and the holder stationary.
Finish straightening the white pen above the empty left portion of the holder opening before lowering it.
Lower the white pen cautiously into the left side of the opening, keeping clear of cyan and avoiding a deep push against the cup.
White tip is visibly inside the opening. Release without pushing deeper, then withdraw left and upward to verify it settles in the holder.
White remains in the holder. Move the open left hand toward the black pen, beginning a top-down approach while maintaining right-hand support.
Continue toward the black pen with open jaws and gradual downward rotation, keeping a controlled elbow-up approach.
Finish the downward orientation and position the left jaws over the upper body of the black pen before the final descent.
After the continuity interruption, retract slightly and lower while using half-size wrist increments. Reapproach the black pen from the accepted elbow-up branch.
Advance slowly over the black pen while completing the last small downward wrist adjustment, keeping the fingers open for centering.
Replan from the rejected forward step: keep the accepted wrist orientation, retract slightly for reach margin, and lower slowly around the black pen's body.
Stop descending at contact. Close the centered left fingers around the black pen and test lift while retracting from the reach limit.
Black pen is retained. Lift and retract toward the left receiving approach, gradually rotating it upright while the right hand supports the holder.
Carry the black pen above the receiving area and continue straightening it, keeping clearance over the two pens already in the holder.
Finish straightening the black pen over an empty part of the opening, with a small leftward centering adjustment before descent.
Lower the upright black pen toward the empty left side of the cup opening, stopping short of a deep insertion to avoid disturbing the other pens.
Seat the black pen tip just inside the opening, release without a deep push, and start withdrawing the left fingers to check that it remains.
Three pens remain in the holder. Purple is in the right workspace; prepare a lower left-hand support grasp on the holder so the right arm can recover it without crossing.
Lower the left gripper below the right-hand grip, then approach the holder's lower body from the left with open jaws for a supported handoff.
Advance the left fingers around the lower holder body and close for support, retaining the right grasp until the handoff can be checked.
Keep the lower left grasp closed; open the right hand and withdraw outward slowly to test that the filled holder remains supported by the left hand.
Left hand now supports the holder. Shift it into the left receiving area while the free right hand rises and begins orienting for the fallen purple marker.
The prior command executed zero steps. Use quarter-size right-wrist increments to leave the wrist singularity, while slowly shifting the left-held cup left.
Finish positioning the left-held cup in its receiving workspace. Approach above purple with the free right hand and gradually orient the jaws across the marker.
Keep the three-pen holder supported by the left hand. Move the open right jaws above purple and continue aligning for an overhead grasp.
Continue pitching the right jaws downward above purple, lowering only slightly until the marker is centered in the wrist view.
Finish the overhead orientation above purple and descend to a pre-grasp height. Left hand keeps the three-pen holder fixed.
Purple is centered between the right jaws. Descend slowly to surround its body before closing, holding the cup steady with the left hand.
